production_changes.watchdog_owner: One ActionClosureWatchdog is created by run_live_scientific_campaign, passed through every bound episode and StageDScientificReplayEnv, bound to the task runtime, and completed or failed once at campaign scope.
production_changes.composition_adapter: _ScientificReplayWatchdog is the single private mode adapter. Its mode is taken from the authenticated StageDScientificEpisodeBinding; QA provider calls are closed/cancelled and rejected, while execution provider and child-gather calls delegate to ActionClosureWatchdog.
production_changes.controller_hooks: Both replay controllers expose provider and concurrent-child hooks required by the pinned prepared-observer path; controller finalization still asserts ExactSamplingDirector drain.
production_changes.phase_order: QA readiness remains before run_eval; provider/child calls are watchdog-owned; finalization and receipt append are inside the finalizer phase after controller, trace, terminal-reply, reward, and evidence checks.
production_changes.finalizer_ownership: Finalization validates controller/trace state before starting one StageDReceiptLedger-owned transaction. Preparation runs in a disposable ledger copy; the live ledger is changed only by a short-lived child process under an authenticated transaction manifest. The manifest's committed state is the linearization point. A timeout terminates with a 0.1-second grace, kills and reaps within a 2-second bound, removes only its authenticated new record/evidence paths and temporary stages, and leaves the parent writer closed fail-closed; any post-commit acknowledgement, cleanup, verification, or apply failure also irreversibly closes and poisons the writer until a fresh authenticated reopen resolves the committed manifest. No synchronous ledger fsync runs on the event loop and no worker survives.
production_changes.transaction_security: The v2 transaction request, result, manifest, and cleanup messages use exact canonical key sets and domain/schema bindings with separate request, result, cleanup-request, and cleanup-result size limits; cleanup accepts the request hex envelope at its independently derived bound. Root, ledger ID, genesis digest, transaction, operation, request/result, immutable baseline, and child patch hashes are authenticated. Root and every existing ancestor are rejected when symlink/reparse-linked. Paths are restricted to exact records/evidence names and transaction-specific temporary names beneath the bound ledger root; aliases, baseline files, substituted temporary bytes, and pre-existing transaction temporaries cannot be removed. Recorded actions are parsed by the exact BehaviorAction/ExactActionKey schema and domain owner, with canonical bytes and recomputed digest validation, not a caller-supplied minimal envelope. The parent exchanges only bounded canonical stdin/stdout bytes with an isolated Python -I child using the fixed repository source root, with no pickle, inherited test hook, caller commit gate, or caller-supplied request path. Request creation, commit, rollback, verification, cleanup, and fsync operations are owned by bounded child processes; malformed or unanchored state is poison/fail-closed.
production_changes.fixture_binding: The source-free QA fixture derives each frozen BehaviorAction from the exact replay task, FixtureRenderer output, resolved sampling, split_engine_sampling result, and TrainClient prepared request; _require_prepared_action remains unchanged.
production_changes.target_id: scientific_env validates the selected target ID as exactly one nonempty str without an untyped return.
production_changes.readiness_guard: StageDReceiptLedger continues to require completed source rollout, frozen roster, exact target membership, correspondence, recorded-action digest equality, no prior QA/scientific activity, and zero generated/judge cost.
production_changes.compatibility: _OneTaskset exposes the pinned Taskset.task_type owner required by Verifiers serving; no protocol or receipt schema changed.
